key_insight: EvoPINN turns PINN design into an execution-grounded search problem, using an LLM agent to discover valid, PDE-specialized training algorithms automatically.
engineering_relevance: This could reduce manual trial-and-error in scientific simulation workflows by producing more robust PINN formulations for solving PDEs in solid mechanics and related domains.
method: Decouples neural representations from training programs to create a modular search space.
Uses an LLM agent to propose iterative, memory-conditioned program modifications.
Filters candidates with strict structural verification and budget-matched PDE evaluation.
evidence_signal: Across oscillatory, elliptic, dissipative, and nonlinear transport PDEs, the method reports lower relative L2 error than baselines and preserves gains under parameter-matched comparisons.
watch_item: Performance depends on strict verification and fair evaluation budgets, so gains may be sensitive to search constraints, benchmark choice, and implementation details.
paper_title: EvoPINN: Agentic Discovery of Executable Algorithms for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
